Here's something most people never think about. When you push down the lever on a toaster, it doesn't actually know when your toast is done. It's just running a timer, and it has no idea what's happening to the bread. That's why the same setting gives you perfect toast in the morning and charcoal an hour later. The toaster is already warm, so the bread browns faster, but the timer doesn't know that. Which, frankly, is a little bit silly.

I want to talk about the little cup on the dishwasher door, the one that pops open halfway through the cycle. A lot of people don't realize there's a second, smaller spot right next to it, and it's there for a reason. That's for the pre-wash. If you leave it empty, the first part of the cycle is basically just splashing water around. Put a little detergent in there, and suddenly your dishwasher works a whole lot better. You're welcome.
